Notice that the quadratic factor in the denominator has a negative discriminant:

$$
D={1}^{2}-4(1)(1)=-3<0
$$

So, we proceed with the following partial fraction decomposition:

$$
\frac{3{x}^{2}+2x+1}{x({x}^{2}+x+1)}=\frac{A}{x}+\frac{Bx+C}{{x}^{2}+x+1}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,B,$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $x({x}^{2}+x+1),$ and we get

$$
3{x}^{2}+2x+1=A({x}^{2}+x+1)+(Bx+C)x.
$$

Solving for the unknown constants using the usual methods, we get $A=1,B=2,$ and $C=1.$ Therefore,

$$
\frac{3{x}^{2}+2x+1}{x({x}^{2}+x+1)}=\frac{1}{x}+\frac{2x+1}{{x}^{2}+x+1}.
$$

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{3{x}^{2}+2x+1}{x({x}^{2}+x+1)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{x}+\frac{2x+1}{{x}^{2}+x+1})\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{2x+1}{{x}^{2}+x+1}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

For the first integral, we have

$$
\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|.
$$

For the second integral, we use the substitution $u={x}^{2}+x+1.$ Then $\text{d}u=(2x+1)\,\text{d}x,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2x+1}{{x}^{2}+x+1}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{u})\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|u| \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|{x}^{2}+x+1| \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+x+1).\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{3{x}^{2}+2x+1}{x({x}^{2}+x+1)}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{2x+1}{{x}^{2}+x+1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|+\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+x+1)+K\end{aligned}
$$
